items.stem: A Go program launches one goroutine per incoming request with no limit and eventually exhausts memory under load. What is the most appropriate fix?

options.text: Bound concurrency with a worker pool or semaphore channel
options.rationale: Correct: limiting the number of concurrent goroutines caps resource use under load.
Forcing GC does not address the unbounded number of live goroutines.
Larger buffers do not limit how many goroutines are created.
defer is unrelated to the number of goroutines spawned.

items.explanation: Correct: limiting the number of concurrent goroutines caps resource use under load.

items.stem: Two slices were created by slicing the same underlying array. Writing through one changes the other. What explains this?

options.text: Slices share the same backing array unless explicitly copied
options.rationale: Correct: a slice is a view over a backing array; sub-slices share that storage.

options.text: Go passes slices by reference like pointers to the same struct
options.rationale: Slices are passed by value, but the value includes a pointer to shared backing storage; the precise cause is the shared array.

options.text: Maps and slices are the same type in Go
options.rationale: Maps and slices are distinct types with different semantics.

options.text: The garbage collector merged the two slices
options.rationale: The GC does not merge distinct slices.

items.explanation: Correct: a slice is a view over a backing array; sub-slices share that storage.

items.stem: Which TWO practices help write correct concurrent Go code? (Select TWO)

options.text: Run tests with the -race flag to detect data races
options.rationale: Correct: the race detector surfaces unsynchronised concurrent access.

options.text: Use a context to signal cancellation and deadlines
options.rationale: Correct: context propagates cancellation so goroutines stop promptly.

options.text: Share mutable state across goroutines without synchronisation
options.rationale: Unsynchronised shared mutable state causes data races.
Dropping errors hides failures and leads to incorrect behaviour.

items.explanation: Correct: the race detector surfaces unsynchronised concurrent access.
